text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp. said Wednesday it has begun a review that may result in job cuts at its corporate headquarters in downtown Pittsburgh and its Energy Systems headquarters in nearby Monroeville, Pa.
The review is related to Westinghouse's sale of its defence electronics and office furniture units within the past year, said company spokesman Kevin Ramundo.

The jobs under review are "related to support activities and general administrative activities" and include the company's legal, communications, strategic planning and environmental affairs departments, he said.
A Orlando, Fla., power generation facility is also under review, and employees were notified this week, Ramundo said.

"The industry and technology group is a smaller and much more focused group than it was a year ago," he said. "We have a resulting opportunity to take a look at how we provide support services, and perhaps do it more cost efficiently."
Any jobs that are eliminated will be phased out by the end of the year. The review covers all 500 workers at corporate headquarters and about 500 workers at Energy Systems headquarters.

The review does not affect Westinghouse's plan to separate its industrial and broadcast businesses, Ramundo said. The company, which acquired CBS Inc. last November in a $5.4 billion deal, is expected to outline its separation strategy in the fourth quarter.
Ramundo said there is no target number of jobs to be eliminated. Westinghouse has reduced its workforce by about 24,600 employees since 1993.
Westinghouse's stock rose 37.5 cents to $18.25 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
